April 26, 40.
Great China University (大夏大學) - Situation

Unrest now exists in the Great China
University, Lane 1081, House 1051 Bubbling Well
Road, where the pro-Wang Ching Wei clique and the
pro-Chungking Government clique are at loggerheads.
So far as is known the situation is as follows :
The Great China University was founded in
1924 by Messrs. WONG PAH CHUN (王伯群),
ex-Minister of Railways of the National Government,
EUR YUAN HWAI (歐元懷), WONG TSE WEI (王毓祥)
and FOO SUH YEH (傅式說). Following the
withdrawal of the Chinese forces from the Shanghai
area, Messrs. WONG PAH CHUN and EUR YUAN HWAI,
respectively President and Vice-President, left
for Kweiyang, Kweichow Province, to take charge
of the administration of the Great China University
in that city.
Mr. FOO SUH YEH, one of the founders, then
assumed the control of the institute in Shanghai in
the capacity of acting president, with Mr. LU CHI
TSUNG (魯繼曾) as Dean and concurrently Chief
Secretary. The school was removed from its former
premises at Chungshan Road to 197 Route Ghisi in
September, 1938, but due to objections by the
French Municipal Authorities, it was transferred
to the Shanghai Girls' University, 451 Taku Road.
Subsequently, the university was further removed
to the present address at Lane 1081, House 1081,

Bubbling Well Road, while the middle school
department is located at 725 Avenue Foch, French
Concession. Altogether there are some 1,000
students and 50 teaching staff in this school.

In the latter part of 1939, Mr. FOO SUH YOH,
the acting president, formed connections with the
Wang Ching Wei clique and through his efforts, a
number of professors and students of the university
have joined the Wang's party. Several professors
belonging to Wang's clique have left the school
ostensibly on leave, but the following are serving
in the new Central Government at Nanking :

Mr. FOO SUH YOH - acting president, now Minister
(傅式說) of Railways of the new Central
Government.

Mr. POH YUE - professor of literature, now
(卜 愈) Secretary to the Ministry of
Railways of the new Central
Government.

Mr. TSANG SOO MING - Chief of the Customs
(張素民) Inspectorate of the Ministry
of Finance of the new Central
Government.

Mr. NYI'EN UNG TSOH - reported to be serving in the
(嚴恩祚) Ministry of Finance of the new
Central Government.

Mr. TSANG FOH - professor of Social Science,
(章 後) reported to be serving in
the Ministry of Railways of
the new Central Government.

Following the appearance of pro-Wang Ching
Wei elements, Mr. LU CHI TSUNG, Dean and Chief
Secretary, was instructed by the President, Mr. WONG
PAH CHUN, to take charge of administration of the

Great China University in Shanghai, and to guard
against the extension of influence by the pro-Wang
Ching Wei elements in the institute. However,
Mr. LU appears to be facing difficulties in respect
of administration of the school, as Mr. FOO SUH YOH;
now Minister of Railways of the new Central
Government, is known to be in control of the
financial affairs of the university.

Recently, a "School Support Committee" is
reported to have been formed by students of pro-
Chungking Government clique to counteract the
activities of pro-Wang Ching Wei elements.
Discreet enquiries have failed to reveal the names
of principal leaders, but it is learned that the
movement is connected with Mr. CHIANG CHIEN PAH
(蒋建白), member of the Education Mission for
Shanghai, which was appointed by the National
Government in February, 1939.

At 9a.m. 15.9.39 the undersigned interviewed Mr.Lu
Chi Chen at his home and learned that he had made
enquiries among the supporters of both the National
Government and the Reformed Government. He was given
to understand by the former that he was in good standing
and his removal from office was not contemplated. From
the latter, through Mr.Fu Shi Yueh, he learned that none
of the various factions desired him to leave Shanghai or
had entertained any suggestion of assassinating him;
however, the actions of certain pro-Teng Ching Wei groups
who were described as "rascals", could not be guaranteed
as their positions were held mostly by actions showing
their loyalty to the movement.

It is worth noting that whilst Mr.Lu Chi Chen and
Mr.Fu Shi Yueh are politically opposed, they are good
friends in private life.

At 3.30p.m. 13/9/39 Mr. Lu Chi Chen (魯繼昌)
Chief Secretary and Dean of the Great China University
Lane 1699/1001 Bubbling Well Road, brought to Bubbling
Well Station two threatening letters:-

(a) a letter from the Iron and Blood Corps stating
that as a traitor to China he
would be "found"
dead. Received by the complainant on
13/9/39 but not handed to the Police until
13/9/39. Contents are not legible.

(b) a piece of paper bearing the following
under headings:- (1) Leave Shanghai immediately.
(2) three lines in outline with the top one
crossed out. (3) five small circles. In the
bottom left corner "Association for clearing up
political scum, 4th;" signed and chopped "Wong Lih."
This letter was posted in the Bubbling Well
Postal District on 12/9/39 and received by the
complainant at 4p.m. 13/9/39.

The complainant cannot identify the writing in
either letter. He has political associations, being
a former member of the Shanghai Municipality Bureau
of Education, and being the dean of the Great China
University (Shanghai Branch) which has its parent
body in Kweiyang, Kweichow.

The daily movements of the complainant coincide
approximately with general office hours, but he
travels on foot from his home at Lane 1699/3 B'Well
Road to Avenue Haig (St. George's) where he boards

With reference to Diary No. 1, Mr. Lu Chi Chen
(魯繼曾) imparted to the undersigned certain
information which in his view must be regarded as strictly
confidential.

Concerning the establishment of the Great China
University, Mr. Lu Chi Chen stated that it was founded
in 1924 by three professors from Amoy University named
Mr. Ou Yuan Hwai (歐元懷), Mr. Wang Chu Wei (王祉偉)
and Mr. Fu Shi Yueh (傅式說) who is also known as Tsoo
Ying (竺隱). The first two completed their studies
in America and the last in Japan.

Until the outbreak of Sino-Japanese hostilities
in August 1937, the university was situated at the
intersection of Chapei and Great Western Roads. The
Principal was Mr. Tang Teh Chun (王伯羣). The
undersigned was one of the secretaries and also a member
of the Shanghai Municipality Bureau of Education. After
the outbreak the university moved into the interior. Mr.
Ou Yuan Hwai, Mr. Wang Chi Wei and Mr. Lu Chi Chen went
with it, but Mr. Fu Shi Yueh stayed in Shanghai.

The university was re-established in Kweiyang,
Kweichow Province, with Mr. Ou Yuan Hwai as Principal.
Mr. Wang Chi Wei proceeded to Chungking as a member of
the Nationalist Government's Legislative Yuan.

At the same time, Mr. Fu Shi Yueh established a

2252' 39    B'w.

1e/2.

branch of the university on Toku Road and about
September 1938 moved it to its present site at Lane
1081/1051 Bubbling Well Road.
        Mr. Lu Chi Chen proceeded to Kweiyang during
August 1937 and returned to Shanghai during April 1938
after consulting the faculty of the university concern-
ing the way in which the Shanghai Branch should be
conducted.    Due to his fears that the branch might
lose its patriotic spirit, Mr. Lu Chi Chen went to
Kweiyang in August 1938 and returned in June 1939 with
written authority to take over the positions of Chief
Secretary and Dean; this so that the Nationalist
character of the branch might not be impaired.
        Concerning Mr. Fu Shi Yueh, he was known to be
sympathetic to Japan and a supporter of Mr. Wang Ching
Wei.    He slowly reduced his activities in the
university and recently took an active part in the
local meeting of Kuo-Ming-Tang officials who adhere to
the policy of Mr. Wang Ching Wei.    According to the
complainant, Mr. Fu Shi Yueh is of such importance that
his name is not mentioned in connection with the new
party.
        Considering that the university is pro-
Nationalist, it is possible that the forceful elimina-
tion of the complainant would cause the greater part of

Translation

To my little boy Chi Chen,

You frequently visited Shanghai and Kweiyang.
We have made investigation and know what you have done.
You, being a chief-secretary and a dean of an university,
have attempted to be a traitor, enticed students with money
to join your party, held up the management of the university,
kept in touch the bogus organisation and spoiled the war-
resistance. You were formerly the officer i/c of the
Education Bureau of Shanghai, and our Government has not
treat you badly. Why have you become crazy and changed your
mind? You have behaved so bad that we are very angry with
you. You had better leave Shanghai immediately and return
to Kweiyang, and you will then still be a professor of an
university, otherwise your deadbody would lie across a street.
Don't blame us for not having advised you before hand.

(Sd.) Iron & Blood Traitors-
Assassination Corp.
